environment.load_generator: the experiments' requests come from the same machine

experiments.title: A worker dies in the middle of payments
experiments.fault: 100 payments whose first provider call fails; while both order-worker replicas work through them, one is killed (SIGKILL)
experiments.hypothesis: No payment is lost and none is charged twice: RabbitMQ redelivers the unacknowledged jobs to the other replica, and the provider gets the task id as its idempotency key.

observations.label: Charges at the provider
observations.value: 100 charge ids for 100 payments: none charged twice

observations.label: Redelivered to the other worker
observations.value: 1 job(s) the killed worker held unacknowledged

experiments.title: Kafka is down while orders come in
experiments.fault: Kafka stopped; 10 orders created; Kafka started again
experiments.hypothesis: Orders are still accepted at full speed: each event waits in the outbox, in the same transaction as its order, and every consumer group catches up once Kafka is back.

observations.label: Orders accepted while Kafka was down
Every consumer group caught up after Kafka was back

experiments.title: RabbitMQ is down
experiments.hypothesis: Only queued work is refused, with 503 and Retry-After; reads and orders keep working; once RabbitMQ is back the API and the workers reconnect by themselves.

observations.label: A new job while RabbitMQ is down
Jobs accepted again, without a restart
That job done by a reconnected worker

experiments.title: Redis is down
experiments.hypothesis: The API fails fast and honestly (503 with Retry-After, readiness down) instead of erroring or hanging, and serves again as soon as Redis is back.

observations.label: A request while Redis is down
A sandbox from before the restart
observations.value: 401: gone with Redis, as designed (nothing personal is kept)

observations.label: An order right after the restart
observations.value: its trace completed in 0.5 s: every service reconnected
